6FC2.text: Faction sheets will name a specific Treachery card (or cards) that a player can choose to discard in order to use their Karama power. They may still only trigger this effect once per game, and they may not discard the specified card(s) to cancel any other faction's advantage (as if using an actual Karama card).

8ACX.text: Example: House Atreides have their Golden Path Karama Power. In the Spirit World variant House Atreides would be able to activate this by using either a Karama Card or the Family Atomics card.

8U43.text:
The following one\-time ability is triggered by playing a Karama card:

Look at any one player's entire Battle Plan (not just your opponent). This cannot be canceled by Karama.

Spirit World Variant: Family Atomics.
8U43.title: Karama power - Golden Path:

AAAX.text:
The following one\-time ability is triggered by playing a Karama card

During the Revival Phase revive up to four forces (including Sardaukar) and one leader for free. These revivals do not count against your normal revivals for the round.

Spirit World Variant: Cheap Hero.
AAAX.title: Karama power - War Machine:

ECM6.text: Note: This variant was originally considered an optional rule in the 1979 edition of Dune, and part of the "Advanced" rules in the 2019 edition.

GTRQ.text: This variant gives each faction an additional way to trigger their once\-per\-game Karama power.

NZBC.text: Karama is a Fremen word meaning miracle, or an action initiated by the spirit world.

P96D.text: A Karama effect is not triggered when the Spirit World card is otherwise discarded normally, and one faction cannot discard another faction's Spirit World card in order to trigger the effect for them.

SQPV.name: Fremen battle edge:
SQPV.text: If using Spice Dialing, the Fremen Battle Edge advantage is changed to mean they are always considered full strength, without needing spice.

Y2MQ.text: The Emperor has a greater chance of triggering their Warmachine Karama Power since there are multiple copies of Cheap Hero in the Treachery deck.

BRZ9.name: Call sandworms:
BRZ9.text: During the Spice Blow and Nexus phase, all subsequent Shai\-Hulud that appear after the first one drawn that phase may be placed by you in any sand territory you wish at the end of the Nexus, devouring any spice or opposing forces there. If placed in a territory where you or your ally have forces, they may Ride the Worm.

C3TF.name: Fedaykin:
C3TF.text: Your three starred forces, Fedaykin, are worth two normal forces in battle and in taking losses. They are each treated as one force in revival; however, only one Fedaykin force can be revived normally per round (except by use of the Tleilaxu Ghola Treachery card).

CLYJ.name: Battle edge: vulnerable to Karama
CLYJ.text: You do not spend spice for spice strength, but automatically gain the spice strength simply by dialing the required number of forces.

FH7K.name: Indigenous:
FH7K.text: Your reserves are already on\-planet; you do not ship using off\-planet shipment rules. For your Force Shipment, deploy any or all of your reserves for free into The Great Flat or directly into any one territory within a distance of two territories of The Great Flat (subject to storm loss and occupancy rules).

K2BB.text: Vulnerable to Karama: Karama may be played while Battle Plans are being formed. If this advantage is canceled by Karama, you may still spend spice normally for spice strength.

NDG3.name: Fremen strategy:
NDG3.text: Your major handicap is poverty. Usually you can't purchase Treachery cards for several rounds, since the others will outbid you. You must be patient and move your forces to spice blows or any vacant strongholds, keeping your force strength high. When you do battle, you can afford to dial high and sacrifice your forces, since they have a high revival rate and you can bring them back into play at no cost.

QAPT.text: Call a Shai\-Hulud during the Spice Blow and Nexus phase. This is counted as if Shai\-Hulud was drawn, but you immediately decide if sandworms appear in the territories of the last Spice Blows card, or if a sandworm will be placed in any sand territory by you at the end of the Nexus (as if using Call Sandworms).

QNZA.name: Sandwalk:
QNZA.text: During your Force Movement you may move your forces two territories instead of one.

QRAS.name: Wormriders:
QRAS.text: If Shai\-Hulud appears in any territories where you have forces, they are not devoured. Upon conclusion of the Nexus, you may "Ride the Worm", moving some or all of the forces in those territories to any territory subject to storm loss and occupancy rules (any spice or forces in the destination territory are not destroyed).

RZCU.name: Karama power - Bless The Maker:
RZCU.text: The following one\-time ability is triggered by playing a Karama card:

C6KB.text: The Treachery deck contains Weapons, Defenses, Actions, and Worthless cards. Other than the card(s) a player starts with, generally the only way to gain them is in the Bidding phase.

HEUH.name: Worthless
HEUH.text: Worthless cards provide no effects normally, and they can only be discarded from a player's hand by being played in a Battle Plan in lieu of a weapon and/or a defense (unless an effect specifies otherwise). Once revealed in a Battle Plan, they must be discarded.

KUYJ.name: Weapons and defenses
KUYJ.text: There are three types of weapons and defenses: kinetic, poison, and special. Some expansion special weapons are also considered the other types as well, indicated in their sub\-title (e.g., Weirding Way). Weapons and defenses are only played in Battle Plans when a faction is in a battle. Weapons in a Battle Plan will kill an opposing leader (even a Cheap Hero) if not protected by an appropriate defense. For example, a kinetic weapon is blocked by a kinetic defense. Some special weapons are only blocked by a specific defense, or cannot be blocked at all.

YYN9.text: When a faction wins a battle, a weapon and/or defense played in their plan may be retained and used in future battles (even in the same round), unless otherwise indicated. A player may always choose to discard any of the cards in their Battle Plan, even when they win a battle.

ZXM2.name: Actions
ZXM2.text: These cards provide a one\-shot effect, and they are always discarded after their effect is fully resolved. Only Family Atomics is removed from the game after being played. If an Action card indicates it is played in a Battle Plan, it can only be played in that manner, and is always discarded, even if that player wins the battle.

2BY9.name: Capture leaders: vulnerable to Karama
2BY9.text: When you win a battle, you may choose to capture a leader from your opponent. Randomly select 1 available leader (including the leader used in the battle, if not killed, but excluding all leaders used elsewhere that round, already captured, or in the Tleilaxu Tanks). After secretly looking at the captured leader you must decide to either 1) place the leader in the Tleilaxu Tanks to gain 2 spice from the Spice Bank; or 2) keep the leader behind your Screen for a one\-time use in any of your battles. If used in a battle, and not killed, you must then return that leader to its faction. The identity of the captured leader is not required to be revealed.

3RX4.text: Vulnerable to Karama: Karama may be played to cancel your Capture Leaders advantage immediately after you win a battle, but before the captured leader is drawn.

44MJ.text: When all of your own Leader discs are unavailable to you (killed, captured, or face up on the board from previous battles), you must immediately return all captured leaders to their factions. Killed captured leaders can be revived by their factions (subject to the normal revival rules). Captured leaders used in battle may still be claimed as a Traitor (subject to the normal Traitor rules): If you use a leader against its own faction and they are holding that leader's Traitor card as a [uncertain: "safe leader"], it may be revealed as a Traitor, winning them the battle in accordance with normal rules for revealing a Traitor.

4QZ3.name: Traitors:
4QZ3.text: At the start of the game, keep all 4 Traitor cards you are dealt. If you have drawn any of your own leaders, you may reveal some or all of them, and then set them aside. Before any other Traitor cards are returned to the Traitor deck by other players, redraw that many cards from the Traitor deck if possible. Keep the new ones, even if any are your leaders, and then shuffle the set aside cards back into the deck.

CUV5.name: At start:
CUV5.text: 10 forces in Carthag, 10 forces in reserves (off\-planet), 10 spice, and 2 random Treachery cards.

HHB4.text: The Harkonnens, led by the decadent and notoriously cruel Baron Vladimir Harkonnen — master of treachery and sinister deeds, value power over all. The path to power leads to Arrakis, and the control of spice.

NJFB.name: Treachery:
NJFB.text: Your hand limit is 8 Treachery cards; when you have 8 Treachery cards you must pass during bidding. Every time you buy a Treachery card you must take an extra Treachery card for free from the top of the Treachery deck unless it would put you over your hand limit.

WGMV.name: House Harkonnen strategy:
WGMV.text: Your major handicap is your difficulty in obtaining spice. You are at your greatest relative strength at the beginning of the game and should capitalize on this fact by quickly buying as many Treachery cards as you can, and then surging into battle, or better yet, extorting spice from other factions. Since you get two cards for every one you purchase, you can afford to bid a little higher than most.

ZWB6.name: Karama power - vendetta:
ZWB6.text: The following one\-time ability is triggered by playing a Karama card:

9TYX.text: However, players can agree to suspend any or all elements of a "thrown battle" over which they have control (e.g., killing a leader, playing a Worthless card, etc.), or add other terms.

AW6B.text: A player cannot make a deal or bribe that would contravene the rules or the player's faction advantages. These are the only limitations.

item-0.text: Each player may play a Leader disc face up.

item-1.text: No forces are dialed (unless a faction must dial to exceed their opponent's leader strength).

item-2.text: No player will call Traitor or use faction advantages such as Capture Leader (or expansion effects like reveal a Face Dancer, Execute a leader, conduct an audit).

item-3.text: No weapons or defenses are included in Battle Plans.

item-4.text: Worthless cards may be played and discarded.

item-5.text: Tech token transfer is optional (if using this variant).

FVFM.text: Spice transferred as part of a deal or bribe is placed in front of the recipient's Faction Screen, by their Faction marker. Players may collect spice from in front of their Faction Screens and add it to their normal spice only at the start of each round's Mentat Pause phase. Bribes may never be made during the Mentat Pause.

H69R.name: Bribery and deals
H69R.text: Players can make any kind of verbal deals or bribes between one another unless allied. Once negotiated, the terms of these deals and bribes must be stated aloud, and must be honored. A player cannot renege on a deal or bribe, and deals are not required to include a spice bribe. If part of a deal becomes impossible to honor, then that part of the deal is void. All parties of a deal may agree to nullify the deal at any time. While players in an alliance can make deals, they are not binding and cannot involve the transfer of spice between them, but they can include normal legal payments (e.g., paying for an ally's Treachery card in the Bidding phase).

H9RX.text: Other player elements are public knowledge, including number of available forces in reserves, and how many special forces are in a territory. Any time a player wishes to secretly share information, it must be made public that this information exchange is taking place.

LZBW.name: Negotiated surrender
LZBW.text: Factions may agree on a thrown battle. When both parties agree, the following is typically true for both players:

RL7Z.text: All spice holdings should be kept behind the Faction Screen. The number of Treachery cards held must be kept open during the Bidding phase, but can be kept secret at all other times.

SALY.name: Faction advantages
SALY.text: Each player's Faction Sheet outlines the unique advantages they may leverage throughout the game. If an advantage uses the word "may", it is optional. Refer to the Faction section (page 27) for specific details about each faction.

XE3H.text: A deal or bribe cannot involve the transfer or gift of Treachery cards, leaders, forces, tokens, or faction advantages (unless specifically indicated). This leaves secret information, stronghold blocking, future actions, and, of course, spice.

XVXK.name: Secrecy
XVXK.text: Players are never required to keep their cards, spice holdings, available leaders, or the traitors they selected secret. They also are not obligated to reveal this information either (except as part of a deal \- see below).

ZERT.name: Sharing information
ZERT.text: Information in Dune is a valuable resource, and it can be offered in deals (including as bribes).

8VSZ.name: Leaders
8VSZ.text: One Leader disc is secretly chosen and placed face [uncertain: up in] the slot on the Battle Wheel. Players may play a Cheap Hero Treachery card in lieu of a Leader disc.

AFGL.text: Example: Atreides have 4 forces in a battle. They can dial any number from 0\-4. If they win the battle, they will lose the strength they dialed (in their case, the number of forces lost will be the number they dialed). If they lose, they will lose all of their forces.

item-0.text: Leaders that survive battles may be played in further battles in the same territory, but no leader may fight in more than one territory during the same phase (except when a traitor is called \- see below).

item-1.text: If possible, a player must always play a Leader disc as part of their Battle Plan if they have one available unless playing a Cheap Hero.

item-2.text: If a player cannot play a leader (including a Cheap Hero) they do not need to announce so prior to revealing Battle Plans.

ETJW.text: If three or more players are in the same territory, the player with Initiative picks who they will battle first, second, etc. for as long as they have forces in the territory.

item-0.text: Players cannot battle one another in a territory if only one player's forces are in storm or if forces are on opposite sides of the storm. Their forces remain in the same territory at the end of the phase. Forces in storm in the same sector of a rock or stronghold territory still battle.

item-1.text: Players cannot battle in Polar Sink. It is a free haven for everyone, and any number of factions may have forces there. Note that if a token is in Polar Sink, creating a "territory within a territory" (e.g., the Ixians' Hidden Mobile Stronghold), forces must battle in that territory within Polar Sink.

FHLW.text: To resolve a battle, each player secretly formulates a Battle Plan. A Battle Plan always includes the amount of force strength dialed on the Battle Wheel. If possible, it must include a Leader disc or a Cheap Hero Treachery card. Additionally, it may include Treachery cards at the player's discretion.

KSES.name: First player (and initiative)
KSES.text: When resolving battles, the First Player has "Initiative" until all of their battles, if any, have been fought. The player with Initiative chooses the order in which they wish to fight their battles. They may even choose a battle in a non\-stronghold territory where they must fight two or more rivals, then choose a different territory before returning to the original territory to battle other rivals there.

LHF2.name: Battle determination
LHF2.text: Wherever two or more players' forces occupy the same territory, battles must occur between those players. Even forces in a different sector of the same territory are considered part of that battle (unless separated by the storm). Battles continue until only one player's forces (or no forces) remain in each territory on the map with two exceptions:

RM6U.name: Force strength
RM6U.text: Each player in the battle takes a Battle Wheel and secretly dials a number from zero to the amount of force strength they have in the disputed territory. This is typically the number of forces a player has there (but with double\-strength special forces, it is their value\- see below). Regardless of the battle's outcome, they will lose at least the amount of force strength dialed on the Battle Wheel. A faction will lose all of their forces in the territory if they lose the battle.

SEWY.text: Then the player to their immediate right gains Initiative and so on, following storm order, until all battles are resolved.

XF89.text: Players in the same territory must battle until no territories are co\-occupied.

49PD.text: Additionally, there is a yellow line starting at Broken Land, going down around the Polar Sink, around Cielago West and out by Habbanya Erg. This indicates where the Fremen can make their Force Shipments to.

5CSY.text: There are six player circles around the map to help determine play order. The map also includes a Round Track and the Tleilaxu Tanks for holding dead leaders and forces awaiting revival.

AEUS.text: The game includes 2 Battle Wheels, which must be assembled and joined with the center pin before you play the game.

HW4P.text: Some territories are marked with a Spice Blow icon to show the locations of possible Spice Blows.

item-0.text: Sand: Yellow or tan with a single border.

item-2.text: Strongholds: Red brown with triple borders.

item-3.text: Polar Sink: Mottled white with a double border.

T6ZH.text: Round track · Spice Blow · Territory · Tleilaxu Tanks · Longitude lines · Sector · Spice Bank · Player circles

W7TV.text: The map is also divided by longitude lines into eighteen sectors, which extend from the edge of the Polar Sink to the equator at the edge of the board. Sectors control the way the storm moves around the board. Note that some territories can span more than one sector.

W8TD.text: The game board is a map of the planet Dune showing four types of territories:

N7TE.text: The Fremen, represented by the planetary ecologist Liet\-Kynes — commanding fierce hordes of natives, adept at life and travel on the planet, and dedicated to preventing any outside control while bringing about Dune's own natural regeneration.

DXLF.name: Bidding
DXLF.text: During the Bidding phase, allies may help each other by paying some or all of the cost of each other’s Treachery cards. To do so, they pay the necessary balance to the Spice Bank (by either paying the full amount, or whatever amount is left after what their ally was willing or able to pay). Players cannot bid more than the total of the spice they have, plus the spice that their ally is willing to contribute to help pay for a card. If a player agrees to let their ally bid higher, they are committed to spending the spice if their ally wins the bid, or guaranteeing the bid.

PLHD.name: Alliance abilities
PLHD.text: Allies may assist one another as specified on their Faction Sheets and Alliance cards.

U8EZ.name: Shipment
U8EZ.text: During the Shipment and Movement phase, allies may pay for each other's shipments. To do so, they pay the necessary balance (by either paying the full amount, or whatever amount is left after what their ally was willing or able to pay).

4959.text: Several years passed and stories began to filter back to the Baron. The program was not proceeding as well as expected. There were reports of raids of increasing intensity on the outlying villages conducted by specially trained Fremen troops called Fedaykin. These raiders were inflicting many more casualties than they were receiving, and the harvesting of spice was beginning to suffer. Especially alarming were the reports of a messianic leader called Muad'Dib who was organizing, training and leading these Fremen to victory after victory. The cutback in spice was beginning to cause serious repercussions throughout the Imperium. A decision was finally made at the highest level for a cooperative and concerted effort by the Emperor; the Landsraad and the Spacing Guild to aid Baron Harkonnen in destroying the Fremen resistance forever.

37VZ.text: Even as Duke Leto was preparing for his journey to Dune, yet another party was watching the situation very closely. The Spacing Guild had a monopoly on all space transport and along with the Emperor and the Landsraad formed the triumvirate that controlled the Imperium. The Spacing Guild guarded its monopoly zealously as it was its only basis for power. No one could travel anywhere through space except in a Spacing Guild spacecraft. Anyone who infringed upon its monopoly or broke its rules was immediately denied all space transport. The Spacing Guild had just one weakness, it could not navigate in space without the melange spice. It was more dependent upon the spice flow than all the others. They, too, would have to monitor the impending conflict on Dune very closely and, perhaps, even actively interfere if the flow of spice were to be threatened.

L3SM.text: Paul and his mother, Lady Jessica, just barely escaped in an ornithopter, a birdlike flying machine, into the desert. For the Baron, victory was complete. From the triumvirate came a sigh of relief, the internecine squabble had been concluded and even though an important noble had been eliminated, the spice would continue to flow.

NH83.text: As Duke Leto and his forces arrived at their dune residence, Arrakeen, nothing seemed amiss. Every object had been carefully checked for traps and poison by the advance party. Envoys sent to the Fremen reported back favorably in regards to the alliance against the Harkonnens. Perhaps the transfer of power would occur without difficulty after all. Suddenly, the blow struck and it came unexpectedly from within. Dr. Yueh, the family Suk doctor, and one who had undergone Imperial conditioning (the highest conditioning against taking human life), had turned traitor. His training had been subverted by Baron Harkonnen who held the doctor's wife as hostage. The doctor secretly turned off the House shields and drugged the Duke and his family to coincide with the Harkonnen surprise attack. He did his job well and the combination of surprise and the additional Sardaukar force was enough to overwhelm the defenders. The Duke was captured to be delivered to the Baron and many of his forces were killed.

NWF7.text: Meanwhile how had Lady Jessica and Paul fared? Having survived a sand storm and a sandworm, they were trapped by a band of Fremen who, following their law of survival, were about to kill them for their water. Because Paul had been specially trained since birth in weapons fighting, Mentat computing and the Bene Gesserit ways, he demonstrated an extraordinary ability to maintain control of the situation. He and his mother so impressed the band that they decided to take them back with them to their sietch, an underground stronghold where the Fremen made their home. Many centuries before, the Bene Gesserit had prepared the Fremen for the coming of the Kwisatz Haderach by a prophecy. A Bene Gesserit and her offspring would hold the key to the Fremen future. Perhaps these visitors were the fulfillment of the legend. Whether or not they were, their abilities could be used to aid the fight against the Harkonnens.

Q98P.text: The Baron was not finished, though. The Fremen had interfered with his destruction of the Atreides forces by helping the remnants to get away. He decided to get rid of the native scum once and for all and gave his nephew, and Feyd\-Rautha's brother, the 'Beast' Rabban Harkonnen, the power to initiate a pogrom to eliminate the Fremen from the face of the planet. The Emperor even loaned the Sardaukar (still disguised in Harkonnen livery) to help.

8949.name: Killed leaders
8949.text: Killed leaders are immediately placed face up in the Tleilaxu Tanks. The winner of the battle immediately receives spice from the Spice Bank equal to the total fighting strength of all leaders killed in the battle (including their own leader, if killed).

6XZW.text: For example, the Emperor has dialed 3 in a battle where they have three normal forces and three double\-strength Sardaukar forces. They may choose to lose all three normal forces, or they may choose to lose one Sardaukar and one standard force (equaling a total strength of 3 for what they dialed).

PVQG.name: Special forces
PVQG.text: If a winning faction has "double\-strength" special forces in a battle, they may use them to absorb losses based on their number dialed.

QK3L.name: Losing
QK3L.text: The losing player loses all of their forces in the territory to the Tleilaxu Tanks and must discard every Treachery card they used in their Battle Plan.

QS4X.name: Winning
QS4X.text: The winning player loses only the number of forces equal to the strength they dialed on their Battle Wheel (one can still win a battle even if they full\-dial and lose all of their forces). These forces are placed in the Tleilaxu Tanks. If the Treachery card text allows, the winning player may keep or discard any of the cards they played. These cards may be used in a subsequent battle, even in the same round, and even in different territories.

TKLE.name: Surviving leaders
TKLE.text: Surviving leaders are placed face up in the territory where they were used until all battles in other territories have been resolved. Note that these leaders may be used again in any battles in that same territory. If a player picks up a leader for a subsequent battle in that territory, they need not use that same initial leader in battle, but must set all leaders used in that territory face up after the battle (if surviving). At the end of the phase, they are retrieved by their owners.

Z7MG.text: Note that the loser does not automatically lose their leader as a result of the battle's outcome; leaders are killed only by Weapon Treachery cards without the proper defenses. Even if the losing player successfully killed the winning player's leader, they do not collect spice.

2AB8.name: Transmutation:
2AB8.text: You may use a Worthless Treachery card as a Karama card, canceling another faction's vulnerable advantage.

69A7.text: The Bene Gesserit Sisterhood, represented by Reverend Mother Gaius Helen Mohiam — ancient and inscrutable, carefully trained in psychological control and a genius at achieving her ends through the efforts of others.

6HFF.text: The next four pages contain a copy of the Faction Sheets for you to reference during your games.

8L3M.text: Alternatively, you may use a Worthless card as a Solaris card to buy a Treachery card for free when it is your turn to bid, allow any faction to ship at Spacing Guild shipping rates when they make a Shipping action, paid to the Spice Bank, or pay the cost of your spice strength in a battle from the Spice Bank.

AA32.name: At start:
AA32.text: After Fremen placement (if in the game), start with one force token in any territory of your choice. If alone, place it as a fighter; if sharing a territory with another faction, place it as an advisor.

HQB2.text: Vulnerable to Karama: Karama can be played to cancel this effect immediately after you have declared how you intend to use Voice.

JQPB.name: Charity:
JQPB.text: You always receive CHOAM Charity of 2 spice regardless of how much spice you already have. This amount increases or decreases if any effect modifies CHOAM Charity.

KRZL.text: You are adept in the ways of mind control.

ND4M.name: Voice: vulnerable to Karama
ND4M.text: You may force your opponent to play or not play any Treachery card matching a general type you name of weapon or defense (kinetic, poison, or special) in a Weapon or Defense slot in their Battle Plan. Other cards that could be played in a Battle Plan are not affected by Voice (e.g., Cheap Hero, Worthless cards, or Reinforcements). A card that is labeled as both special and kinetic/poison is affected by either command (e.g., Shield\-Snooper). If your opponent cannot comply with your command, they do not have to admit their inability to comply and instead may do as they wish.

S4SK.name: Prediction:
S4SK.text: After step 1 of Game Setup (Positions), you secretly predict when one other specific faction will win, placing a Round Number card and a Faction card from your Prediction cards face down behind your Faction Screen. Place the unused Prediction cards face down back in the box. If the faction you predicted wins (alone or as an ally, even your ally) in the round you predicted, reveal your Prediction and win alone. You also can win normally. You cannot predict a win achieved via an advantage titled "Special Victory Condition".

V9M7.text: 19 forces in reserves (off\-planet), 5 spice, and 1 random Treachery card.

X2DQ.text: Your strengths are that you have the ability to deploy forces for free each round as advisors, and you can win by correctly predicting the round another player will win the game and then secretly working for a favorable outcome. In addition, you can be quite effective in battles by voicing your opponent and leaving them weaponless or defenseless.

XRUX.name: Bene Gesserit strategy:
XRUX.text: Your major handicaps are your low revival rate and having very little income. You should not allow large numbers of your forces to be sent to the Tleilaxu Tanks or you may find yourself without sufficient reserves to bring onto the planet.

82YK.text: With access to ornithopters now, the Spacing Guild makes a Force Movement, moving forces from Tuek's Seitch to Cielago South in order to harvest the spice there.

FAFJ.name: Spacing Guild movement example
FAFJ.text: Example: On their turn, the Spacing Guild makes a Force Shipment of 1 force into Arrakeen to gain access to Ornithopters.

RC34.text: With so many House Atreides forces in Arrakeen, it would have been safer to ship forces into Carthag where there is only 1 Bene Gesserit force, however they can't ship forces into a sector in storm.

QR4V.text: The Spacing Guild, represented by Navigator Edric, monopolist of transport, yet addicted to ever increasing spice flows, must ensure that trade continues unabated.

26DB.text: In all subsequent Storm phases, the storm's movement will be determined by drawing a Storm card and advancing the Storm marker from its current position counter\-clockwise around the map the sum total of sectors.

2FTC.name: First storm
2FTC.text: During the Storm phase of the first round, place the Storm marker at a random location along the map edge using the following procedure: the two players whose Faction markers are nearest on either side of the Storm Start sector secretly dial a number from 0 to 20 on the Battle Wheels. The two numbers are simultaneously revealed and totaled, and the Storm marker is moved from the Storm Start Sector counter\-clockwise around the map the sum total of sectors. There can be no coordination between these two players about where the initial Storm marker will end up being located.

5S2U.text: One Storm card calls for the last two players to handle Battle Wheels to dial the storm (each a distance of 1\-3 sectors). That would typically be the two players who fought the last battle in the previous round. If no battles were fought in the previous round, use the two players on either side of the storm's current location (and if it is located exactly at a player's Faction marker, use the two factions on either side of that faction). Unlike the first storm's positioning, players may make deals or bribes about how to dial for this card's effect.

AD92.text: If Family Atomics is used to destroy the Shield Wall, the storm does not immediately kill forces in Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin if located over those territories before moving. Those forces will be lost whenever the storm moves over or ends its movement over those territories.

EHHL.text: The Storm marker will be moved a random number of sectors around the board (if any), potentially changing which player will go first in each applicable phase, and blocking sections of the board (including a stronghold on occasion).

GWK9.text: Play proceeds counter\-clockwise (or in "storm order") from the First Player.

LDK4.name: Storm cards
LDK4.text: When a Storm card is drawn, it forms a discard pile, meaning most of the time a different Storm card will be drawn in the next round. However, three of the Storm cards have a "Reshuffle" instruction on them. After the storm has moved, shuffle all of the discarded Storm cards back into the deck.

P5NL.name: First player
P5NL.text: The player whose Faction marker the storm next approaches is the First Player in the Bidding phase, Revival phase, Shipment and Movement, and Battle phase. If the storm is directly even with a faction Marker, then that player is last in storm order for any phase that has player turns.

XW8B.name: Destruction
XW8B.text: Any forces in a sector of sand territory (except the Imperial Basin while Shield Wall is intact) over which the storm passes or stops are destroyed. Place destroyed forces in the Tleilaxu Tanks. Forces that are not in sand territory find protection from the storm. In addition, any spice in a sector of sand territory over which the storm passes or stops is removed to the Spice Bank.

22ZV.text: For example, Atreides gains Treachery card knowledge during the Bidding phase, and they can solicit bribes to share that information to some or all of the other players. It is allowable for Atreides to simply show the actual card up for bid to any player, whether as part of a deal or for any reason.

5YXW.text: For example, "I won't attack you in Hagga Basin if you bribe half of that spice when you harvest it".

9LEX.text: Another example: House Harkonnen keeps all the Traitor Cards they draw. The Harkonnen player may sell some or all of that information to another player, providing possible safe leaders to play.

MHWK.name: Taking notes (and discard piles)
MHWK.text: Players are not permitted to keep notes, other than Atreides' advantage for Bidding. The contents of discard piles are not public information, and no discard pile may be searched unless an effect allows a player to do so.

VB78.name: Social interaction
VB78.text: Dune at its best is highly social. Players are encouraged to threaten, intimidate, bargain, and bluff about every aspect of gameplay. Reason with the other players to do or not do particular actions, whether it's self\-serving or mutually beneficial.

73QN.caption:
The Emperor is in a battle with House Atreides.

They dial 6 force strength and pay 4 spice to add +2 spice strength.

They play Hasimir Fenring who is a 6 strength leader.

This gives them a battle total of 14 strength.

The Emperor plays a Snooper poison defense and a Baliset to complete their battle plan
73QN.title: Emperor Battle Plan

2M87.text: For thousands of years, the religious and semi\-mystical sisterhood of the Bene Gesserit had groomed the peoples of the Empire to prepare for a messiah, a Kwisatz Haderach. To achieve this end, they had trained themselves to influence and impress the people by a combination of religious mysticism and the power of their Voice \- the ability to control others merely by selected tone shadings of their voice. They also had secretly conducted a rigorous and careful genetic program to match mates with the ultimate object of producing a Kwisatz Haderach \- one who through his genetically developed ability to contact higher dimensions could utilize the insights gained to bring a new order to the universe.

6F3H.text: The Atreides family had governed the planet, Caladan, for twenty generations. In that time, their continued impartial and efficient leadership had earned for them the respect of their noble peers throughout the Imperium and, gradually, they began to acquire more and more influence in the noble assembly, the Landsraad. The present head of the Atreides family, Duke Leto, had just been selected as the unofficial spokesman for the Landsraad, its highest position.

8WTV.text: The Bene Gesserit were upset with one of their sisters, the formal concubine to Duke Leto Atreides, Lady Jessica. As one of the final agents in their breeding program, she had been instructed to bear a female child who was then to marry Feyd\-Rautha Harkonnen, the Baron's nephew. There was a high probability that a male offspring of that union would be a Kwisatz Haderach. For some reason never quite understood, even by herself, Lady Jessica upset the program by bearing a son. This boy, named Paul, became the direct heir to the Atreides line and, along with his mother, was now accompanying his father to the new planet. The sisters would have to watch the events as they unfolded on Arrakis very carefully or they might just lose their genetic investments.

LQ9M.text: His simplest solution would be to send his fanatical police army, the Sardaukar, to arrest Duke Leto. Unfortunately, the Duke's character was so exemplary that no believable pretext for his arrest could be devised. A more subtle and serviceable plan began to creep into his devious mind. Why not reward Leto for his services to the Empire with a promotion to the governorship of a new and more important planet, Arrakis. He knew that the present governor of Arrakis, Baron Harkonnen, would not give up this planet without a struggle and would prepare a trap to surprise the Duke and his family when most vulnerable \- just after arrival on their new planet. In fact, he would secretly aid the Baron by loaning him Sardaukar disguised in Harkonnen livery. If Duke Leto refused the governorship, he would be ostracized by his fellow nobles and forced to become a renegade. Either way Shaddam IV would be rid of him.

WU85.text: This growing influence of the Atreides was viewed with great concern by a powerful personage of no less rank than the Padishah Emperor, Shaddam IV, himself. Shaddam had grown politically war\-wise in a regime long hoary with intrigue and corruption. The emergence of the upright and charismatic Duke Leto as a powerful leader of the nobility, he realized, could be a very real threat to his own position.
